reading.title: Learning together
reading.text: For decades, children with disabilities were often excluded from mainstream schools and taught separately. Today, most countries support inclusive education, in which all children learn together. A recent review of 40 studies concluded that inclusion benefits not only disabled pupils but also their classmates, who become more tolerant. However, teachers say they need training and extra staff; without them, inclusion can exist on paper only. Several governments have refused to disclose how much they actually spend on support.

items.q: In the past, many children with disabilities were…
What did the review of 40 studies find?
o: Only disabled pupils benefit from inclusion.
